newsitem.title: USA: U.S. banks' Sumitomo deals booked as loans.
newsitem.headline: U.S. banks' Sumitomo deals booked as loans.

text.p: Two U.S. banks that effectively loaned Sumitomo Corp almost $1 billion through copper-linked derivatives booked the trades as loans, a top Federal Reserve Board official said.

Chase Manhattan Corp and J.P. Morgan & Co made the loans in the form of swaps, leaving investigators to ponder if the deals were part of a scheme by former Sumitomo trader Yasuo Hamanaka to manipulate world copper prices.
"It was booked as a loan and follows the capital requirements of loans," Fed Governor Susan Phillips told a Congressional hearing of the House Banking Committee.
"In this case, it turned out that the economics of it were very much like a loan," Phillips said. "Had they not booked it as a loan, I would have been more concerned."
Chase and Morgan officials declined an invitation to appear at the hearing, but bank officials gave the committee a private briefing, chairman James Leach said.
Phillips said the banks structured the loans as derivatives to satisfy Sumitomo's desires.
"This was an effort for the banks to try to structure financing of these very complicated transactions to try to facilitate the customer's needs," Phillips said.
"This is an example of banks trying to facilitate international trade activities," she said.
Phillips said the banks appear to have set aside adequate capital reserves for the positions. Sumitomo has met all its obligations to the banks so far, she said.
The Fed is not interested in micromanaging the banks' loan departments, Phillips emphasized.
"If we try to proscribe particular types of loans that they should make, I think we'll all be getting in over our heads," Phillips said.
